GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Hand-rolled port of PhrogParasite.cs:39-53. The REACHABLE graph is a two-node alternation: INFECT_MOVE (initial) <-> LASH_MOVE, wired by the FollowUpState assignments at :45-46. The 'RAND' RandomBranchState built at :44 and given two CannotRepeat branches at :47-48 is never assigned to any FollowUpState and is not the initial state, so it is dead in the game as well. The port alternates deterministically and draws nothing. Executed, not asserted (verdict rule 5): `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain` rebuilds the C# GenerateMoveStateMachine graph node for node on the sim's OWN MonsterMoveStateMachine primitives (so the walk, the repeat rules and the single-NextFloat(total) draw are the audited machinery) and diffs it against the shipped port over 20 turns from an identically seeded RunRngSet. Result: 20/20 turns identical (INFECT, LASH, INFECT, ...) and 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides -- the zero-draw property is the one that would break first if the port had 'restored' the dead branch.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 4-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 64 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [61,64], observed [61,64], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 64 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
